definition: a short, memorable phrase used in advertising or politics
hook: Slogan began as a battle scream.
modernAnchor: Three words on a billboard, a jingle you cannot shake. We call it a slogan.
journey: Gaelic sluagh meant host or army, and gairm meant a cry, so sluagh-ghairm was the war cry of the host.
Highland clans shouted their rallying cry as they charged, and each clan had its own.
English borrowed it in the 1500s as slogorne, and for centuries it meant only a battle shout.
Around the 1800s the word moved from the battlefield to politics, and later to advertising, where the charge is for your wallet.
